## 173. The Horizons approximation's offset table is interpolated backwards: the offset jumps up to 0.99 mas at every year from 1963 to 2011

**Severity: Correctness (positions under SEFLG_JPLHOR_APPROX, SEMOD_JPLHORA_1 at every date and SEMOD_JPLHORA_3 after 1962, up to 0.99 mas off and discontinuous at each year of the table)**
**Where:** `swephlib.c`: `swi_approx_jplhor()`

Entry 162's noticed item. The Horizons approximation turns a place about
the pole by an offset in right ascension, -51.257 mas before 1962 Jul 1
(`DCOR_RA_JPL_TJD0`), then a table of yearly values, `dcor_ra_jpl[]`, to
2012, and -52.255 mas after. Between two years the code took
(t - t0) (v[t0] - v[t1]) + v[t0], the difference the wrong way round: the
offset ran from v[t0] away from v[t1], ended the year at 2 v[t0] - v[t1],
and jumped by 2 (v[t1] - v[t0]) to the next year's value. The largest
step in the table, -52.292 to -51.796 mas into 2006 Jul 1, made a jump of
0.992 mas: Polaris's barycentric right ascension under SEMOD_JPLHORA_1
moved 2.87e-7 deg in 2^-9 day across JD 2453917.5 beyond its motion,
Mars's 2.76e-7. Between the years the offset was off by up to that much
too. Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:** linear between the years' values, (t - t0)
(v[t1] - v[t0]) + v[t0], behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`. The places
are continuous across the table's years to the stencil's own error (Mars
2.0e-12 deg, Polaris 2.9e-10 through its speed). The offset's rate, now
the table's slope, stays out of the speeds, at most 3.8e-10 deg/day
(entry 162). No hot path: the approximation's own branch.

G141 `tests/jplhorbias.c`, extended with 2 checks: Polaris's and Mars's
right ascension under SEMOD_JPLHORA_1 at the start of each of the table's
49 inner years, the place 2^-10 day after less that 2^-10 day before
less 2^-9 day of their mean speed, the worst within 1e-9 deg. 75 checks.
Before the fix both fail (2.87e-7 and 2.76e-7 at 2006 Jul 1), and so in
the compat build. G24 `jplhora_table_jump`: barycentric Polaris on
de200, across 2006 Jul 1: 1.5e-11 deg shipped, 2.90e-7 compat.

## 164. A JPL file whose `swe_set_jpl_file()` failed along the path then set, and a path where it is: no DE number was read, so the path setter reads none, and the first JPLEPH delta t takes the default tidal term until a calculation opens the file

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: call order -- the first UT JPL Moon in AD 1700 1.79e-3 deg off the second, the first JPLEPH delta t 11.27 s off, `swe_deltat()` 12.08 s off and its guess Swiss for a configuration naming de200.eph -- on every thread and context)**
**Where:** `sweph.c`: `swe_set_jpl_file_r()`, `swe_set_ephe_path_r()` (bug 148's condition), `ctx_release()` (bug 131's); `sweconfig.c`: `swi_config_capture()`, `swi_config_apply()`, `cfg_merge()`, `swi_config_reset()`; `sweph.h`, `sweconfig.h`

Entry 148's noticed item. Bug 148 has `swe_set_ephe_path()` read the kept
JPL file again along the new path, and bug 131 has the first entry after
`swe_close()` read it, when a DE number had been read for it
(`jpldenum_cfg`, or owed since a close). A `swe_set_jpl_file()` that
failed along the path in effect read none, so neither fired. After a path
without de200.eph (a /tmp directory of links to EPHEDIR's other files),
`swe_set_jpl_file("de200.eph")` and the path to EPHEDIR: `swe_calc_ut()`'s
JPL Moon in AD 1700 40.0057507520 deg on the first call and 40.0039614086
on the second, which the first had opened the file for; `swe_deltat_ex()`
there with SEFLG_JPLEPH 14.286718 s (the default term) and `swe_deltat()`
15.091463 s (its guess Swiss, the moon file's -25.936); after a TT JPL Sun
the getter -25.936 and `swe_deltat()` in AD 1800 18.902020 s. A fresh
process given EPHEDIR and de200.eph answers 40.0039614086 twice, 3.012003
s for both delta t, -23.8946 and 14.438958 s. The same on the setting
thread, a thread running across the path, a thread started and a context
made after it, and an explicit context. And with `swe_close()` for the
path: the directory without de200.eph, the failed setter, de200.eph then
linked into it and `swe_close()`: the same values, where a fresh process
given that directory and de200.eph answers as above. The configuration did
not record that a file had been named: the name alone cannot say so -- it
starts as `SE_FNAME_DFT`, and a calculation's fallback to de406.eph
rewrites it. The compat build the same (40.0057510966, then
40.0039617599), as entry 148's.

**Fix, as done here** (under `SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`'s `#ifndef`; the compat
build keeps upstream's first and second answers):
- `swe_set_jpl_file()` marks the file named (`jpl_named`), found or not.
  The flag is in the configuration's path group with the name: captured,
  merged, compared and adopted as the name is, so a thread adopting the
  setter or a later path and a context made after carry it; the compat
  build never sets it.
- Bug 148's condition in the path setter, and bug 131's in `swe_close()`
  (`ctx_release()`, and `swi_config_reset()` for the master), is that
  flag: the named file is read again along the new path, or owed to the
  next entry after the close, as a fresh process's `swe_set_jpl_file()`
  reads it whether or not an earlier one found it.
- The opens, `fopen()` interposed, 100 rounds after the setters and a
  warm-up, before and after: a path alternating between EPHEDIR and
  EPHEDIR/. and a JPL Moon each round, 200 calls and 100 opens of
  de200.eph both (the setter's open replaces the calculation's); with a
  Swiss Moon each round 300 calls and no open before, 400 calls and 100
  opens after, as a process given EPHEDIR and de200.eph from the start
  makes (400 and 100); with the named file nowhere along the path, 300
  calls before and 400 after, one failed attempt per path change, which a
  fresh process's setter makes there too. No hot path.

G132 (`tests/jpldenum.c`, entry 137) gains two settings: the first path a
directory without de200.eph and the last setter the path to EPHEDIR, and a
second such directory, de200.eph linked into it and the last setter
`swe_close()`, each against a fresh process given the final path and
de200.eph: 7 settings x 5 readers x 5 observations and one check, 176
pass. Before the fix 30 fail, 15 in each setting, on all 5 readers alike:
the JPLEPH delta t, the getter after the JPL Sun with `swe_deltat()` in
1800, and the first Moon, as above. The compat build fails 85 of 176 with
the fix and without: entry 148's 55 of 126, and in the two settings 30 by
the upstream behaviour it restores, the first JPLEPH delta t and the first
Moon (bug 148's, 10 each) and the flag-0 delta t (bug 145's, 10). G24
`jpl_named_moon_off`, the first UT JPL Moon in AD 1700 after the
directory without the file, de200.eph and EPHEDIR against the second: 0
shipped, 1.79e-3 deg compat (and shipped before the fix).

## 165. With no JPL file set, the first JPLEPH delta t takes the default tidal term and the calculation after it opens the default file by its name: the first answer differs from the second, in a fresh process too

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: call order -- the first UT JPL Moon in AD 1700 1.79e-3 deg off the second where de431.eph is not DE431, the JPLEPH delta t 11.27 s apart before and after a JPL calculation; with de431.eph missing and the fallback's de406.eph, by -25.826 for -25.80, 0.154 s in AD 1700 by the same proportion -- on every thread and context)**
**Where:** upstream `swephlib.c` `swi_get_tid_acc()` (the JPL file's DE number only when it is open), `sweph.c` `open_jpl_file()` (the fallback to de406.eph); here `swephlib.c`: `swi_get_tid_acc()`; `sweph.c`: new `swi_jpl_open_first_use()` and `jpl_open_note_say()`, `open_jpl_file()`, `swecalc()` and `jplplan()` (their opens), `swi_close_keep_topo_etc()`, `ctx_release()`; `sweconfig.c`: `swi_config_apply()`; `sweph.h`

Entry 148's noticed item. With no `swe_set_jpl_file()` the JPL file's
name is the default, `SE_FNAME_DFT` (de431.eph), and nothing has read its
DE number: `jpldenum_cfg` is published by the setter alone (the
2026-09-16 review's F4), and the file is open only once a calculation has
opened it. So a JPLEPH delta t took the default term, -25.80, and the
calculation after it opened the file by its name, its term the file's
from then on. With a de431.eph that is de200.eph (a /tmp directory of
links), in a fresh process given that path alone: `swe_calc_ut()`'s JPL
Moon in AD 1700 40.0057507520 deg on the first call and 40.0039614086 on
the second; `swe_deltat_ex()` in AD 1700 with SEFLG_JPLEPH 14.286718 s
before any JPL calculation and 3.012003 after a JPL Sun; the same on a
thread running across the path, a thread started and a context made
after it, and an explicit context. Where de431.eph is missing and
de406.eph is there, the calculation's fallback opens de406.eph ("Error
with JPL ephemeris file de431.eph: ... Defaulting to de406.eph", only when
there is a serr to write it in) and rewrites the name: the same two
Moons with that warning on the first, where de406.eph is de200.eph; with
a real DE406 its -25.826 for -25.80, 0.154 s of delta t in AD 1700 and
2.4e-5 deg of the Moon by the same proportion (no DE406 file here). With
a real DE431 file the term is the default's, and no answer moves. The
compat build the same (40.0057510966, then 40.0039617599).

The decision. The default name does not count as named for bug 164's
flag: the path setter would then open de431.eph at every path change for
every caller, or try it where none is installed (a failed `fopen()` per
path element), and the guess (`swe_deltat()`, and the functions without a
flag, bug 132) would turn JPL wherever a de431.eph is found, DE431's
-25.80 for the Swiss files' -25.936 (11.29 s of delta t in AD 1000), for a
configuration that names no JPL file (entry 138: a calculation does not
choose for the guess). The file a JPLEPH request uses is the default
file, or its fallback, along the path: its DE number is read where it is
first needed, as bug 107 reads the moon file's at the first tidal term.

**Fix, as done here** (under `SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`'s `#ifndef`; the compat
build keeps upstream's first and second answers):
- `swi_get_tid_acc()`, for SEFLG_JPLEPH with no DE number -- no file
  open, none published -- opens the file first
  (`swi_jpl_open_first_use()`), as the calculation would: its name along
  the path, and the fallback to de406.eph only when the delta t has a
  serr, as the calculation's open falls back only with one (in
  `swe_calc_ut()` and the other UT functions the two are the same
  buffer). The file stays open for the calculation, which opens nothing
  then. The guess stays Swiss; nothing is published (F4).
- The fallback's warning, which the calculation's own open wrote, is
  written into the delta t's serr and kept for the calculation that finds
  the file open (`jpl_open_note`, emptied by every open), which writes it
  where its open would have (`jpl_open_note_say()` in `swecalc()` and
  `jplplan()`): `swe_calc()` clears serr at its start, so the first
  `swe_calc_ut()` would otherwise have lost it.
- Where the file is not found the delta t answers as before, the default
  term, without the open's error in its serr, and does not try again
  until a file opens or a setter, `swe_close()` or an adopted path or
  file changes what would be found (`jpl_first_missed`); the calculation
  retries its own open at every call, as upstream's does. A default name
  tried with no serr has not tried de406.eph, so that miss is not kept.
- The opens, `fopen()` interposed, before and after: the path whose
  de431.eph is de200.eph and two UT JPL Moons, 1 call and 1 open both;
  100 more, none both; 100 rounds of a path change and a JPL Moon, 200
  calls and 100 opens both; with a Swiss Moon, 300 calls and no open both;
  the de406.eph fallback and two Moons, 2 calls and 1 open both; no JPL
  file anywhere, the fallback allowed, two UT JPL Moons 6 .eph calls
  before and 8 after (the first delta t's try of de431.eph and de406.eph)
  and 100 more 300 both. The resolver is on the hot path, the new branch
  only for SEFLG_JPLEPH: calc-swieph 12266746003 instructions before and
  12266746129 after, calc-moseph 23333308548 and 23333308874.

G132 (`tests/jpldenum.c`, entry 137) gains three settings with no JPL file
set: the path a directory whose de431.eph is de200.eph and no last
setter, or the path again by another string, or the first path a
directory with no JPL file (its readers asking a JPLEPH delta t too) and
the last setter the de431.eph directory, each against a fresh process
given the final path alone: 10 settings x 5 readers x 5 observations and
one check, 251 pass. Before the fix 18 fail: the first Moon on all 5
readers in each setting (15), and with no last setter the JPLEPH delta t
3.012003 s for the fresh process's 14.286718 on the 3 readers that
computed a JPL Sun first. The compat build fails 137 of 251 with the fix
and without: entry 164's 85 of 176, and in the three settings 52 by the
upstream behaviour it restores (the first Moon, 15; the JPLEPH delta t,
7; the getter and `swe_deltat()` after a JPL Sun following the open file,
bugs 103 and 138, 15; the flag-0 delta t, bug 145's, 15). The fallback's
warning does not fit G132's bit-for-bit serr (a reader that opened the
file before reports nothing), so G24 takes it: `jpl_dft_moon_off`, in a
forked child called first, the first UT JPL Moon in AD 1700 against the
second along the de431.eph-is-de200 path, and after `swe_close()` along a
path without de431.eph whose de406.eph is, the larger, 1 if the first
call's serr lacks the fallback's warning: 0 shipped, 1.79e-3 deg compat
(and shipped before the fix); with the warning not carried to the
calculation, 1.

## 166. Without the moon files the Swiss files' tidal term is the default, not the planet files' DE number's: delta t 11.29 s off in AD 1000, and every answer that keeps SEFLG_SWIEPH with it

**Severity: Correctness (residual above the floor: delta t 0.037 s off at 1900 and 11.29 s in AD 1000; the heliocentric Mars 2.6e-7 deg off at 1900 and 5.8e-5 in AD 1000, the mean apogee 4.9e-8 at 1900, with the fallback the Sun 4.4e-7 and 1.3e-4 -- on every thread and context)**
**Where:** upstream `swephlib.c` `swi_get_tid_acc()` (SEFLG_SWIEPH's DE number from the moon file alone); here `sweph.c`: `ephe_path_read_moon()`, new `ephe_path_read_planet()`, `ctx_release()`; `swephlib.c`: `swi_get_tid_acc()`; `sweconfig.c`: `swi_config_capture()`, `swi_config_apply()`, `cfg_merge()`, `swi_config_reset()`; `sweph.h`, `sweconfig.h`

From PR #33's list of defects found and not fixed. The Swiss files' term
is the moon file's DE number: the open moon file's, else the one the path
setter read from semo_18.se1's header and published (bug 101's
`sweph_denum_moon`). With no moon file along the path there is neither,
and the term was the default, `SE_TIDAL_DEFAULT`, -25.80, DE431's. The
planet files there are DE441's: sepl_18.se1's header, like semo_18.se1's,
names DE441, `SE_TIDAL_DE441` -25.936 (the finder's figure; -25.80 is
DE431's, the default's). Measured with a /tmp directory of links to
EPHEDIR's files but semo*.se1, against EPHEDIR: `swe_get_tid_acc()`
-25.80 for -25.936; `swe_deltat_ex()` with SEFLG_SWIEPH in AD 1000
1463.430567 s for 1474.717432, at 1900 -1.990764 for -1.953326 (0.037 s);
under the strict setting, which refuses what depends on Moshier's Moon
(bug 120), `swe_calc_ut()`'s heliocentric Mars at 1900 286.446337609530
deg for 286.446337869546 (2.6e-7) and in AD 1000 110.447311102471 for
110.447369542638 (5.8e-5); with the fallback allowed `swe_nod_aps_ut()`'s
mean node and apogee at 1900 259.161307172549 and 154.332767121104 for
259.161307149613 and 154.332767169674 (2.3e-8, 4.9e-8: the finder's 5.0e-8
is the apogee's), the Sun 280.153361019726 for 280.153361460308 (4.4e-7)
and in AD 1000 1.3e-4 deg off. The same on a thread, a context and a first
use by `SE_EPHE_PATH`, and in the compat build, upstream's.

The term, on its science. The tidal term in delta t is the Moon's secular
acceleration, n-dot, of the lunar ephemeris: delta t before the
telescopic era is reconstructed from eclipse and occultation timings
reduced with a lunar theory of one n-dot, and `adjust_for_tidacc()`
rescales it to the n-dot of the ephemeris in use (by -0.000091 (n-dot -
n-dot0) (Y - 1955)^2 s), so that this ephemeris reproduces the observed
events. The n-dot belongs to the whole DE integration the files were made
from -- the Moon's orbit was integrated with it, and the planets' with
that Moon -- and the planet files carry its DE number in their header as
the moon files do. Without the moon files:
- the Moon is Moshier's, a theory fitted to DE404 (swemmoon.c), whose term
  is `SE_TIDAL_DE404`, -25.58 (`SE_TIDAL_MOSEPH`). Since bug 120 it answers
  SEFLG_MOSEPH, and `swe_calc_ut()` takes Moshier's delta t for it: its
  term is its own theory's already;
- what keeps SEFLG_SWIEPH comes from the planet files -- the planets, the
  Sun, the Earth but for its 1/82 lunar offset (bug 120's 3.4e-8 deg) --
  or from no file at all (the mean elements): the delta t the complete
  directory gives them is the planet files' DE441 term, and nothing in
  them is fitted to any other;
- -25.80 is the term of no file present, the default for want of one.
So the term is the planet files' DE number's. It is a defect, above the
residual floor (5.0e-8 deg at 1900, 5.8e-5 in AD 1000).

**Fix, as done here** (under `SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`'s `#ifndef`; the compat
build keeps upstream's default term):
- `ephe_path_read_moon()`, when the moon file's header is not found at
  J2000, reads the planet file's there (`ephe_path_read_planet()`:
  sepl_18.se1 opened and its header read as the moon file's is, kept open
  for the calculations with the span it answers for, bug 89's). Its DE
  number is published with the path (`sweph_denum_planet`), captured,
  merged, compared and adopted with the moon file's and owed with it after
  `swe_close()`, so the setters, bug 107's first use, bug 131's reading
  again and a thread or context taking the path all carry it; 0 when the
  moon file's was read. The same path again with its planet file open
  keeps the number read with it.
- `swi_get_tid_acc()` takes it for SEFLG_SWIEPH after the open moon file
  and the moon file's published number.
- After the fix the directory without the moon files answers delta t, the
  getter, the heliocentric Mars and the mean points bit for bit as
  EPHEDIR; the Sun with the fallback 1.55e-9 deg off it at 1900 and
  8.7e-9 in AD 1000 (the Earth's Moshier lunar offset, bug 120's).
- The opens, `fopen()` interposed, 100 rounds after a warm-up, before and
  after: a path change and the heliocentric Mars at 1900 each round, 400
  calls and 100 opens of sepl_18.se1 both (the setter's open replaces the
  calculation's); a path change and a Moshier Mars, 100 calls and no open
  before, 200 and 100 after, as EPHEDIR's setter opens semo_18.se1 for its
  header (100 and 100); the same path again and the heliocentric Mars, 100
  calls (bug 118's look for a moon file installed since) and no open both.
  EPHEDIR's counts unchanged. Instructions: calc-swieph 12266746129 before
  and 12266751448 after, calc-moseph 23333308874 and 23333313678.

G142 `tests/moonlesstid.c`, each case in a forked process: the directory
without the moon files read by the setting thread, a thread started after
the path, a thread running across it, a context made after it, an
explicit context, a first use by `SE_EPHE_PATH` and the setting thread
after `swe_close()`; under the strict setting the getter, delta t in AD
1000 and 1900, `swe_deltat()`, the heliocentric Mars at 1900 and in AD 1000
and the getter again, and with the fallback allowed the mean node and
apogee at 1900 and in AD 1000 and the Moon's return flag (SEFLG_MOSEPH),
each bit for bit as the same reader given EPHEDIR: 14 pass. Before the fix
the 14 fail; the compat build fails the 14 with the fix and without, the
strict 7 by upstream's default term and the fallback's 7 by bug 120's
SEFLG_SWIEPH on Moshier's Moon, which it restores. G24 `moonless_tid_off`,
delta t in AD 1000 along that directory against EPHEDIR, each on a context
made and given its path: 0 shipped, 11.29 s compat (and shipped before the
fix).

Noticed, not fixed: `swe_nod_aps_ut()` of the Moon with SE_NODBIT_MEAN and
SEFLG_SWIEPH, geocentric, along a directory without the moon files is
refused under the strict setting ("Swiss (.se1) Moon file is not
available"), though with the fallback allowed its four points and their
speeds at 1900, AD 1000 and J2000 equal EPHEDIR's bit for bit -- an answer
that does not depend on Moshier's Moon refused (bug 120's rule). And with
both J2000 files missing, semo_18.se1 and sepl_18.se1, and another
epoch's there, the path setter reads no DE number and the first delta t
takes the default term: in AD 1500 291.693033 s, then 294.255183 after a
Swiss Moon there opened semo_12.se1, the first Moon 158.4001317882 deg for
EPHEDIR's 158.4005084277 (3.8e-4 deg); before this entry too.

## 167. `swe_nod_aps()` on Moshier sees the Sun's geocentric points from the Earth

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: a wrong answer, returned OK; the Sun's mean perigee 1.5 deg and 1.02 AU off, its apogee 88.5 deg and 0.96 AU), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entry 149's work. The Sun's geocentric nodes and apsides are the
Earth's orbit (`ipli` the Earth) seen from the Sun and negated: the
points, built heliocentric, are moved to the barycentre by adding the
barycentric Sun, the observer is the barycentric Sun, and the difference,
negated, is the Sun's place at its perigee seen from the Earth. On
Moshier, which serves no barycentric Sun, the points stay heliocentric
(`!(iflag & SEFLG_MOSEPH)` skips the addition), and the same test sent the
Sun to the planets' branch: the observer was the Earth, the point the
vector from the Earth to the Earth's own perihelion, negated. At 2000 Jul
1.5:

| the Sun, geocentric | Moshier | the files' |
|---|---|---|
| mean perigee | 281.4259 deg, 1.9993 AU | 282.9417 deg, 0.9833 AU |
| mean apogee | 191.4583 deg, 0.0531 AU | 102.9417 deg, 1.0167 AU |
| osculating perigee | 281.4572 deg, 1.9993 AU | 283.0042 deg, 0.9833 AU |

Every method alike (0, mean, osculating, SE_NODBIT_OSCU_BAR, the focal
point), SEFLG_TOPOCTR with the site added (the speeds then 1.3e-2 deg/day
off their positions' rate). Heliocentric and barycentric output, and the
Earth's points, are not the planets' branch and were right. Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:**
- On Moshier the observer of the Sun's geocentric points is the Sun, its
  origin (zero), as it is the barycentric Sun on the files; with
  SEFLG_SPEED the same for the observer at t - dt the aberration's rate
  takes.
- Now the Sun's points are the Earth's heliocentric ones of the same
  ephemeris and method at their own distance (4.4e-16 AU) in the opposite
  direction (7.6e-7 deg, the light deflection, which takes the distance),
  on Moshier as on the files; Moshier's mean points are the files' within
  2.9e-6 deg and 2.2e-16 AU (the same elements; the files' observer moves
  with the Sun's barycentric velocity, an aberration Moshier's lacks), its
  osculating points as close as the Earth's (1.2e-3 deg at 2000, 4.8e-2 at
  -3000).
- Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: upstream answers so. No hot path
  (`swe_nod_aps()` is not in the bench).

G143 `tests/nodcentre.c` (new): (a) the Swiss files and Moshier, seven
instants -3000..3000, the six methods, geocentric and topocentric: the
Sun's perigee and apogee against the Earth's heliocentric points, distance
within 1e-12 AU, direction within 1e-5 deg; Moshier's mean points against
the files' within 1e-5 deg and 1e-12 AU; their speeds against five-point
differences over 2^-6 day at binary instants within 1e-10 deg/day and
1e-12 AU/day (measured 2.9e-12, 2.9e-14). 357 rows pass; before the fix
189 fail (the 168 Moshier rows of the first check, 143 deg and 0.97 AU,
the second's 14 and the topocentric 7 of the third), the upstream build
273. G133 (h) no longer skips the Sun's geocentric points: the fallback
answers them as the Moshier request does, bit for bit (8 rows; before the
fix they fail, the Moshier request from the Earth and the fallback, its
flag Swiss, from the Sun). 1080 rows pass; the compat build fails 296.

G24 `nodaps_mosh_sun_off`: the Sun's mean perigee on Moshier at 2000 Jul
1.5, its distance less the Earth's heliocentric perihelion distance: 0
shipped, 1.02 AU compat.

## 168. `swe_nod_aps()` takes its frame and site from the caller's ephemeris bits, not from the ephemeris that answered

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: a wrong answer, returned OK, that depends on call order or on a redundant flag bit; Mars's node 0.13 deg off on a warm fallback, 0.108 deg under SEFLG_SWIEPH | SEFLG_MOSEPH), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entry 149's work. `swe_nod_aps()` builds its points
heliocentric and moves them to the centre asked with the save area's Sun
and Earth: on the files, it adds the barycentric Sun and takes the
barycentric Sun or Earth for the observer; on Moshier, whose origin is the
Sun, it adds nothing and the heliocentric observer is the origin. It chose
between the two by the caller's SEFLG_MOSEPH, and placed a topocentric
site by the delta t of the caller's ephemeris bits, where `swe_calc()`
resolves the bits (JPL, then Swiss, then Moshier) and, after a fallback,
goes on with the ephemeris that answered:
- A Swiss or JPL request fallen to Moshier, the fallback allowed, added
  the save area's Sun to Moshier's heliocentric points and took it for
  the heliocentric observer: zero in a fresh process (the answer was
  Moshier's), another call's Swiss Sun in a warm one. The files of
  1800-2400 alone, after Mars's points at 2000 Jul 1.5, Mars's geocentric
  osculating node at 1500 Jan 1 came out 4.3236 deg, latitude 9.1e-3, for
  Moshier's 4.4536 and 1.4e-4 (0.13 deg); the Moon's heliocentric mean
  node 99.7972 deg for 100.1993 (0.40). The site took the files' delta t
  for Moshier's places, fresh or warm: the Moon's topocentric mean perigee
  there 2.9e-4 deg off Moshier's, Mars's 3.3e-7.
- SEFLG_SWIEPH | SEFLG_MOSEPH, answered from the files, took Moshier's
  frame: Mars's geocentric osculating node at 2000 Jul 1.5 69.7303 deg for
  the SEFLG_SWIEPH request's 69.8382, the barycentric node the
  heliocentric 49.5625 for 49.6398, the heliocentric points without the
  aberration the files' carry (3e-6 deg). And the bits went on, unresolved,
  to `swi_plan_for_osc_elem()`, whose `swi_get_denum()` reads SEFLG_MOSEPH
  first: SEFLG_JPLEPH | SEFLG_MOSEPH on de200, answered from DE200, turned
  the osculating ellipse by the frame bias of DE >= 403, Mars's node 1.5e-4
  deg off the SEFLG_JPLEPH request's (1.6e-4 heliocentric).
Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:**
- One ephemeris bit at the top, by `plaus_iflag()`'s precedence, as
  `swe_calc()` resolves them; no bit stays no bit.
- After the call that sets the save area's Sun and Earth, the frame (the
  barycentric Sun added, the heliocentric observer, the Sun's observer of
  entry 167) and the topocentric site's delta t (and the site's
  acceleration in the aberration's rate) are those of the ephemeris of the
  save area's Earth, the one that answered. A Moon from Moshier on the
  files' Earth, the Moon files alone missing (SEFLG_MOSEPH in its flag,
  entry 120), keeps the files' frame and site, as `swe_calc()` computes it.
- Now the mixed bits answer as the ephemeris they resolve to, return and
  points bit for bit; the warm fallback as the Moshier request in a fresh
  process, bit for bit under SEFLG_NOGDEFL, geocentric, topocentric and
  heliocentric. With the deflection Mars's points stay 3.0e-8 deg off:
  `deflect_light_from()` (sweph.c) takes the save area's barycentric Sun on
  Moshier too, the stale one here, as `swe_calc()`'s own Mars on the same
  warm fallback (1.7e-9 deg); not this entry's.
- Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: upstream answers so. No hot path.

G143 `tests/nodcentre.c` (b): SEFLG_SWIEPH | SEFLG_MOSEPH against
SEFLG_SWIEPH, and SEFLG_JPLEPH with SEFLG_MOSEPH, SEFLG_SWIEPH or both
against SEFLG_JPLEPH (de200), five bodies, three methods, four centres, two
instants, the return and the points bit for bit: 480 rows pass; before the
fix 340 fail (12 deg at most), the upstream build all 340 too (613 of
G143's 837). G133 (f), the files of 1800-2400, warm after the call at the
instant: four calls at 1500 against the Moshier request in a fresh
process, Mars geocentric and topocentric under SEFLG_NOGDEFL and the
Moon's heliocentric mean points bit for bit, Mars geocentric within 1e-7
deg; 8 rows, failing before the fix and in the upstream build. 1088 pass
(the compat build fails 304).

G24 `nodaps_mixed_eph_off`: Mars's geocentric osculating node at 2000 Jul
1.5, SEFLG_SWIEPH | SEFLG_MOSEPH against SEFLG_SWIEPH: 0 shipped, 0.108
deg compat.

## 169. `swe_nod_aps()` reads the centre bits otherwise than `swe_calc()`

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: a centre other than `swe_calc()`'s for the same flags, or none, returned OK; Mars's node 0.077 deg off the barycentric one under SEFLG_HELCTR | SEFLG_BARYCTR), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entry 149's work. `plaus_iflag()` gives `swe_calc()` one centre
for any combination of the bits: SEFLG_TOPOCTR turns SEFLG_HELCTR and
SEFLG_BARYCTR off, SEFLG_BARYCTR SEFLG_HELCTR. `swe_nod_aps()` documents
the centres "like the planetary function swe_calc()" but tested the raw
bits: the observer was the barycentric Sun whenever SEFLG_HELCTR was set,
nothing for SEFLG_BARYCTR without it, the site (its geocentric offset)
whenever SEFLG_TOPOCTR was set, and the Earth only without SEFLG_HELCTR and
SEFLG_BARYCTR. At 2000 Jul 1.5, Mars's osculating ascending node on the
files:

| flags | `swe_nod_aps()` | `swe_calc()`'s centre |
|---|---|---|
| SEFLG_HELCTR \| SEFLG_BARYCTR | 49.5625 deg, heliocentric | barycentric: 49.6398 |
| SEFLG_TOPOCTR \| SEFLG_HELCTR | 49.5625, heliocentric | topocentric: 69.8377 |
| SEFLG_TOPOCTR \| SEFLG_BARYCTR | 49.6387, the barycentric points less the site's offset, no centre's | topocentric: 69.8377 |

On Moshier the first answered its heliocentric points under a barycentric
request (`swe_calc()` refuses it, entry 149), and SEFLG_TOPOCTR |
SEFLG_BARYCTR was refused as barycentric (entry 149) where `swe_calc()`
answers it topocentric. For the Moon, which takes no aberration
geocentric, SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_HELCTR took it as heliocentric. Every
body and method alike; the UT form too. Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:**
- The centre bits as `plaus_iflag()` leaves them, at the top, so every
  test below (the observer, the change of centre, the Moon's aberration,
  entry 149's barycentric refusal) reads one centre: SEFLG_HELCTR |
  SEFLG_BARYCTR is barycentric (on Moshier refused, as SEFLG_BARYCTR is),
  SEFLG_TOPOCTR with either or both topocentric.

**Fix, as done here:** `swi_frame_step_side(ctx, t, h, iflag, which)`
compares the model each function of `which` (`SWI_FRAME_PREC`, `_EPS`,
`_NUT`) takes at t with the one it takes at t + h and at t - h, chosen as
the function itself chooses it (`frame_prec_model()`, `frame_eps_model()`,
`frame_nut_model()`, SEFLG_JPLHOR's models by `frame_is_jplhor()`):
-1 when t + h's differs (difference backward), +1 when t - h's does
(forward), 0 when neither. So every step of the three, with its own
inclusive side, is found where the model changes, and each rate asks for
its own model: the precession's fallback and the site's for the
precession, the obliquity's for the obliquity, the nutation's for the
nutation (no step at 1799 and 2202), SEFLG_SPEED3 for all three. Entry
153's one-sided differences then take each side's rate as at 1962. Behind
`#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`, as entry 153's. The test returns 0 at once
unless the flags take SEFLG_JPLHOR's models somewhere (SEFLG_JPLHOR, or
SEFLG_JPLHOR_APPROX under mode 3); the default models and flags read one
model number and two flag bits, as before.

## 181. The long-term sidereal time integrates the precession through a short-term model's window edges: with IAU 1976 and Vondrak ("0,9,1") +24.0" before 1700, +50.8" at 1776, -22.2" at 2215; with IAU 2006 at 75 centuries 1143"

**Severity: Correctness (with `SE_MODEL_PREC_SHORTTERM` set to IAU 1976, 2000 or 2006 by `swe_set_astro_models()` and the default long-term sidereal time, outside 1850-2050: sidereal time off its own side's model's by up to 50.8" within a century of J2000 -+ 2 centuries and 24.0" at every date before 1700, 1.9" with IAU 2000, 1143" at -5550 with IAU 2006; every house cusp and the topocentric site with it)**
**Where:** `swephlib.c`: `sidt_pra_rate()`, `sidt_pra()`, `sidtime_era_long_deg()`, `sidt_lterm_offset()`, `swe_sidtime0_r()`; `sweph.h`: `struct sidt_pra_table`, `struct sidt_splice_memo`

Entry 160's noticed item. The fork's long-term sidereal time (entry 29),
outside 1850-2050 under `SEMOD_SIDT_LONGTERM`, the default, is ERA(UT1)
plus the precession in right ascension accumulated since J2000,
integrated from the precession matrices `swi_precess()` takes at each
instant and tabulated at nodes a century apart, each with its rate, a
central difference over -+ 50 days (`sidt_pra_rate()`), for a cubic
Hermite between two, then spliced onto IERS 2010 at 1850 and 2050 (entry
25, `sidt_lterm_offset()`). With a short-term model chosen, the
precession steps at the window's edges (entry 160: 0.53" and 0.57" at
J2000 -+ 2 centuries with IAU 1976 under Vondrak, 42" and 107" at -+ 75
with IAU 2006). The edges fall on the table's nodes, whose rate took the
step over 100 days, some 180"/cy (1.5e4"/cy with IAU 2006), and the
cubic carried it a century either side, and through the 1850 splice's
offset, at - 1.5 centuries inside that century, to every date before.
Measured against the default models' ("0,9,9", which hold outside the
window in both), `swe_sidtime0()` with a fixed obliquity and no
nutation:
- "0,9,1": +24.03" at every date before 1700, +48.2" at 1750, +50.78" at
  1776, +39.7" at 1790, +16.9" at 1804, -4.42" at 1831; +26.4" at 2150,
  -22.2" at 2215, -25.7" at 2250, +0.43" from 2300 on (the window's own
  difference from IERS 2010, kept by the 2050 splice);
- "0,9,6" (IAU 2000): -0.90" before 1700, -1.90" at 1776, +0.98" at 2150;
- "0,9,8" (IAU 2006 within 75 centuries): +1142.8" at -5550, +71.1" at
  -5501, -111.2" at -5499 (inside).
Against each side's own model alone ("0,1,1", "0,6,6", "0,8,8" inside,
"0,9,9" or "0,8,8" outside), which is what the precession and obliquity
of date are there, 3.1e-4 deg (IAU 2000) to 0.38 deg (IAU 2006). The
houses' ARMC is this sidereal time; the topocentric site is turned by it,
whose velocity takes the precession's rate of the instant's model (entry
73), so the topocentric Moon's speed was 1.5e-8 to 1.9e-8 deg/day off its
places' rate within two days of J2000 - 2 centuries (de200, delta t
2^-11 day, G139's nine-point reference). Upstream's
`sidtime_long_term()`, kept in the compat build, precesses the mean Earth
at the instant and has no table: its sides are its models' own (outside
the window "0,9,1" within 3e-4" of "0,9,9", from the obliquity of J2000 it
takes at every date).

What is correct on each side: the precession and obliquity of date are,
at each instant, those of the model that holds there, the long-term
model's own outside the window and the short-term model's inside, with
no memory of the other; so the sidereal time is, at each instant, the
sidereal time that model alone gives, spliced as it would be alone. It is
continuous wherever the precession is and steps at the edges with it.

**Fix, as done here:** `sidt_pra_rate()` takes the rate of one model
alone, `model` held at every instant as `get_aya_correction()` holds a
model (both precession entries set to it for its three matrices and put
back), so no edge is in the integrand; the table (`struct
sidt_pra_table`) is keyed by that model, two slots as before; the
sidereal time takes the model `swi_precess()` takes at its instant, TT
(`frame_chosen_model()`, which entry 160 wrote, gives its number), and
the splice offset is that model's at the boundary (`struct
sidt_splice_memo` keeps one per boundary for the long-term model and one
for a short-term model whose window holds it). Behind `#ifndef
SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`, as the long-term sidereal time itself (entry 29):
the compat build keeps upstream's formula.
- After: outside the window the sidereal time is the long-term model's
  own, inside the short-term model's own, bit for bit, at every setting
  above and at every instant G139 (d) takes. At the edges it steps, "0,9,1"
  by +0.128" at J2000 - 2 centuries and -0.433" at + 2, where the equinox
  steps about the pole by 0.529" and 0.573": what is left between them,
  0.40" and 0.14", is the IAU 1976 sidereal time's offset from IERS 2010
  at the 1850 and 2050 splices, which holds inside the window and not
  outside. Mars's hour angle, which the sidereal time continuous across
  the edge stepped by the whole equinox (-0.594" and +0.608" on the Swiss
  files), steps by -0.467" and +0.175".
- The topocentric Moon within 6.0e-10 to 8.6e-10 deg/day of its places'
  rate across J2000 - 2 centuries (4.8e-10 to 6.1e-10 with the IERS 2010
  sidereal time).
- Where no window holds (the default models, "0,9,9", "0,8,8", "0,1,1",
  Owen's, Laskar's, "0,8,9", and "0,1,8", where IAU 1976 long-term wins),
  one table as before: `swe_sidtime()` and the houses' ARMC bit for bit
  the tip's at 400 dates from -11400 to +15400. Cost: `perf stat -e instructions:u`,
  20000 `swe_sidtime()` and `swe_houses_ex2()` with speeds 1452..2400 on
  the default models, 16888547065 before, 16899471275 after (+0.065%, the

## 182. The Horizons approximation's obliquity offset table is interpolated backwards too: the mean obliquity jumps up to 0.44 mas at every year from 1963 to 2011

**Severity: Correctness (the obliquity under SEFLG_JPLHOR_APPROX, SEMOD_JPLHORA_1 at every date and SEMOD_JPLHORA_3 after 1962, up to 0.44 mas off and discontinuous at each year of the table; its rate 1.2e-7 deg/day off for a day after each)**
**Where:** `swephlib.c`: `swi_epsiln()`

Found by entry 163's agent. Under SEFLG_JPLHOR_APPROX, `swi_epsiln()` adds
an offset to the mean obliquity from a yearly table, `dcor_eps_jpl[]`,
from 1962 Jul 1 (`DCOR_EPS_JPL_TJD0`), interpolated as entry 173's offset
in right ascension was: (t - t0) (v[t0] - v[t1]) + v[t0], so each year
ended at 2 v[t0] - v[t1] and the offset jumped by 2 (v[t1] - v[t0]) into
the next. SE_ECL_NUT's mean obliquity on de200 under SEMOD_JPLHORA_1, its
second difference over 2^-10 day at 1972 Jul 1: 1.22e-7 deg (0.44 mas).
`swi_obliquity_rate()`, a one-day difference, took the jump for a day:
1.2e-7 deg/day. Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:** linear between the years' values, behind
`#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`. The second difference at the table's 49
inner years is 2.0e-13 deg at most. The rate's one-day difference now
straddles only the table's change of slope at a year, at most 6.8e-10
deg/day (0.9 mas a year over a day), under the floor; left.

G141 `tests/jplhorbias.c`, extended with 1 check: SE_ECL_NUT's mean
obliquity (it has no speeds), its second difference over 2^-10 day at
each of the 49 inner years' starts, within 1e-9 deg. 76 checks. Before
the fix it fails (1.22e-7), and so in the compat build. G24
`jplhora_eps_table_jump`: at 1972 Jul 1, 1.6e-13 deg shipped, 1.22e-7
compat.

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: a wrong answer for a request fallen to Moshier, returned OK; Mars's osculating node at 1500 Jan 1 1.58e-4 deg off the Moshier request's), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entries 167-169's work. The osculating points are fitted to
the ICRS state `swe_calc()` returns at each instant (entry 108), which
`swi_plan_for_osc_elem()` turns into the J2000 frame by the frame bias when
`swi_get_denum()` gives 403 or more for the flag it is passed: `iflg0`,
whose ephemeris bit is the one asked for. SEFLG_JPLEPH on de200 with the
fallback allowed falls to Moshier inside `swe_calc()` outside de200's
1600-2169, which returns Moshier's state and SEFLG_MOSEPH; the DE number
of SEFLG_JPLEPH was still 200, so Moshier's state was left in DE200's
frame, unbiased, where `swe_calc()` biases a fallen request by the
ephemeris that answered (Moshier, 403). Every osculating point was off the
Moshier request's; at 1500 Jan 1 and 2200 Jan 1 (the larger, longitude
plus latitude):

| osculating | geocentric | heliocentric |
|---|---|---|
| Mars, ascending node | 1.75e-4 deg (1.56e-4 in longitude at 1500) | 1.66e-4 (1.58e-4) |
| the Moon, ascending node | 6.45e-5 | 8.6e-8 |
| Mercury, ascending node | 1.17e-5 | 4.52e-5 |
| Neptune, ascending node | 8.37e-5 | 8.13e-5 |
| Pluto, perihelion | 8.0e-6 | 8.1e-6 |
| the Sun's perigee, the Earth's perihelion | 2.58e-6 | 2.58e-6 |

The bias, 23 mas, over the sine of the inclination on the nodes. The

  bit for bit, every body and method, geocentric, topocentric and
  heliocentric (barycentric both refused, entry 149); de200 inside its
  years, the Swiss files and Moshier as before.
- Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: upstream answers so. No hot path.

## 178. `swe_nod_aps()` gives its heliocentric and barycentric points aberration and the Earth's light deflection, where `swe_calc()` gives those places neither

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: points off the frame of `swe_calc()`'s places at the same centre, returned OK; Jupiter's heliocentric mean descending node at J2000 9.6e-4 deg off, its barycentric speeds 3.4e-2 deg/day; Mars's heliocentric points 4.1e-6 deg), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entries 167-169's work. `plaus_iflag()` sets SEFLG_NOABERR |
SEFLG_NOGDEFL for heliocentric and barycentric output, so `swe_calc()`'s
places there carry neither (its heliocentric Mars is the same bit for bit
with them). `swe_nod_aps()` read only SEFLG_TRUEPOS, SEFLG_NOABERR and
SEFLG_NOGDEFL (and kept the Moon from both, but for the aberration of its
heliocentric points):
- the heliocentric points took the aberration of their observer, the
  barycentric Sun, moving at about 1e-5 AU/day (3e-6 deg; the
  barycentric observer is at rest, its aberration nothing);
- both took `swi_deflect_light()`'s deflection, whose observer is the Earth
  (or the site) whatever the centre: the vector from the Sun or the
  barycentre to the point was deflected as if the Earth looked along it.
  Where that direction passes the Sun as the Earth sees it the
  deflection is the limb's: Jupiter's mean descending node at J2000, at
  280.46 deg with the Sun at 280.37 from the Earth, 9.62e-4 deg.

The Swiss files at 2000 Jan 1.5, 2000 Jul 1.5, 1900 Jan 0.75 and 2050 Jan
1, mean and osculating, the largest against SEFLG_NOABERR | SEFLG_NOGDEFL
(longitude plus latitude):

| points | heliocentric (aberration, deflection) | its speeds | barycentric (the deflection) | its speeds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mercury | 3.21e-6 deg (3.05e-6, 2.75e-7) | 8.7e-9 deg/day | 2.80e-7 | 6.9e-9 |
| Mars | 4.09e-6 (3.05e-6, 1.15e-6) | 2.1e-8 | 1.15e-6 | 2.1e-8 |
| Jupiter | 9.64e-4 (2.85e-6, 9.63e-4) | 4.7e-3 | 8.46e-4 | 3.4e-2 |
| Saturn | 2.10e-5 (2.46e-6, 1.97e-5) | 3.3e-6 | 1.97e-5 | 3.3e-6 |
| Neptune | 5.79e-6 (3.06e-6, 4.04e-6) | 1.4e-7 | 4.04e-6 | 1.4e-7 |
| Pluto | 1.43e-5 (3.27e-6, 1.42e-5) | 1.6e-6 | 1.42e-5 | 1.6e-6 |
| the Sun, the Earth | 3.95e-6 (2.16e-6, 3.72e-6) | 2.5e-6 | 2.83e-6 | 1.4e-6 |
| the Moon | 2.20e-6 (the aberration) | 4.6e-8 | 0 | 0 |

JPL alike; Moshier the deflection alone (its heliocentric observer is the
origin, unmoving), barycentric refused (entry 149). Both builds.

**The right answer.** None of either, as `swe_calc()`. Aberration and
deflection are what an observer sees: aberration the observer's velocity
against the barycentric frame, deflection the Sun's field bending the ray
on its way to the observer. The barycentre is at rest, so its aberration
is nothing; an observer at the Sun's centre sits on the deflecting mass,
where the deflection is not defined, and the formula's Sun-observer
distance is zero. What remains, the Sun's 15 m/s against the barycentre,
would be an aberration of the Sun's motion, which no other place in the
library gives a heliocentric observer: a heliocentric place is a
direction in the barycentric frame from the Sun, not an observation.
Taken alike, a heliocentric planet and its own nodes and apsides are in
one frame. The Earth's deflection on a vector from the Sun was nobody's. The flag itself is left as given,
so a star mode's ayanamsa (the star apparent, as `swe_calc()`'s
heliocentric sidereal places take it: Mars's mean node under True Citra
at J2000 sits on `swe_calc()`'s ayanamsa, 1.3e-3 deg from the
astrometric star's) is unchanged.

**Fix, as done here:**
- After the centre bits are read (entry 169), heliocentric and
  barycentric output takes no aberration and no deflection, the Moon's
  heliocentric points included.
- Now those points are the SEFLG_NOABERR | SEFLG_NOGDEFL ones bit for bit,
  every body and method, the files, JPL and Moshier, `swe_nod_aps_ut()`
  too; geocentric and topocentric points as before.
- Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: upstream answers so. No hot path.

G146 `tests/nodapshel.c` (new): (a) the Swiss files, de200 and Moshier,
heliocentric and barycentric, the Sun, the Moon, Mercury to Pluto, the
Earth and Chiron, mean, osculating, SE_NODBIT_OSCU_BAR and osculating
with SE_NODBIT_FOPOINT, four instants, the default flags with and without
SEFLG_SPEED and SEFLG_TRUEPOS against the same with SEFLG_NOABERR |
SEFLG_NOGDEFL, the return and points bit for bit; (b) `swe_nod_aps_ut()`
alike for the Moon and Mars; (c) the geocentric and topocentric points of
Mars and Jupiter still apparent (4.8e-3 deg at least from the
astrometric). 3520 rows pass; before the fix 1808 fail (1784 of (a),
9.64e-4 deg, and 24 of (b), 4.1e-6), the upstream build 2120. G143 (1453
rows), G133 (1120), G79, G47, G69, G104, G92, G78, G42, G53, G46 and G38
pass.

G24 `nodaps_hel_defl_off`: Jupiter's heliocentric mean descending node at
J2000, the files, the default flags against SEFLG_NOABERR |
SEFLG_NOGDEFL: 0 shipped, 8.22e-4 deg compat (9.62e-4 in the default
build before the fix).

## 180. `swe_nod_aps()` on Moshier builds the Earth-Moon barycentre from a Moon other than the one Moshier's Earth was made with: the Earth's and the Sun's osculating points wobble 8.0e-3 deg with the Moon's inequalities, their speeds 4.7e-8 deg/day off their positions' rate

**Severity: Correctness (Moshier's Earth's and Sun's osculating apsides 8.0e-3 deg off the ellipse of Moshier's own EMB at 2000, 4.1e-2 at -3000, 4.6e-2 at -2700; their longitude speeds 4.7e-8 deg/day off five-point differences of their positions, the distance's 2.5e-11 AU/day), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`, and through it `swe_nod_aps_ut()`

Found by entries 167-169's work, as a speed residual whose epoch it did
not pin down: there is none, it is at every epoch. The ellipse of the
Earth (and so the Sun's geocentric points) is the Earth-Moon barycentre's,
built as the Earth plus the geocentric Moon over 1 + EMRAT. On the files
and JPL the Earth is the EMB less that same Moon's share, and the sum is
the file's EMB. Moshier's Earth is its series' EMB less the short lunar
series' Moon (`embofs_mosh()`, six terms in longitude), and the Moon added
back was Moshier's own, 0.24 deg away at 2000, 1.55 deg at -3000: the EMB
came out 1.3e-7 AU and 3.2e-8 AU/day off the series' at 2000 (7.9e-7 AU,
2.0e-7 AU/day at -3000), in the terms the short series leaves out, 9 to 35
days long. The osculating ellipse amplifies the velocity by about 2 / (v
e): the perihelion wobbled 8.0e-3 deg about the series' EMB's at 2000
(its largest term semi-monthly, 5e-3 deg), 4.1e-2 at -3000, the distance
3.8e-6 and 3.8e-5 AU. The speeds are central differences over +-2^-6 day of those
points (entry 80), and the wobble's third derivative, 1.6e-3 deg/day^3
(the files' 1.0e-5 to 2.2e-5), puts such a difference off the rate by h^2
/ 6 of it: 5e-9 to 6.8e-8 deg/day at every epoch, by where the instant
falls in the lunar terms, not by the year; 4.7e-8 at 3000 on G143's
instants, the latitude's 4.0e-10, the distance's 2.5e-11 AU/day. The
Earth's heliocentric points and the Sun's geocentric and topocentric ones
alike; the files' 3.2e-10 deg/day. Moshier's points against the files',
before and after (60 days from each date, the largest):

| Moshier's Earth, osculating perihelion | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 8.04e-3 deg, 4.0e-6 AU | 9.8e-4 deg, 3.4e-7 AU |

## 175. Without the files for J2000 the Swiss files' DE number is read from none: the first delta t takes the default tidal term until a calculation opens a moon file, the first Moon in AD 1500 3.8e-4 deg off the second

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: call order -- delta t in AD 1500 2.56 s off before a Swiss Moon there opens its file, the first UT Moon 3.8e-4 deg off the second; with the planet files alone the default term throughout, the heliocentric Mars in AD 1500 1.56e-5 deg off -- on every thread and context)**
**Where:** upstream `sweph.c` `swe_set_ephe_path()` (the moon file's header read at J2000 alone); here `sweph.c`: `ephe_path_read_moon()`, new `ephe_path_read_other()`, `swi_ephe_path_none()`

Entry 166's noticed item. The path setter reads the DE number from the
files for J2000, semo_18.se1 (bug 101) and, without it, sepl_18.se1 (bug
166). With neither along the path and other spans' files there (links to
EPHEDIR's files but those two), it read none, and the first delta t took
the default term, -25.80, until a Swiss Moon opened another span's moon
file, whose number the term follows from then on: `swe_deltat_ex()` in AD
1500 291.693033 s, after a Swiss Moon there 294.255183; the first UT Moon
158.4001317882 deg, the second 158.4005084277 (3.8e-4), EPHEDIR's both
times; the getter -25.80 for -25.936 until then. With the planet files of
the other spans alone (no moon file, no sepl_18.se1) no calculation opens
a moon file, and the term was the default throughout: the heliocentric
Mars in AD 1500 59.4283715176 deg for 59.4283871221 (1.56e-5), delta t in
1900 -1.990764 s for -1.953326 (no file there; bug 166's planet-file case
for the other spans). The same on a thread, a context, a first use by
`SE_EPHE_PATH` and after `swe_close()`, and in the compat build,
upstream's. Before entry 166 too.

The number to read. Every file of a set is made from one DE integration,
and its header names it: the 153 .se1 files in ephe/ (sepl, semo and seas,
all 51 spans) name DE441. The term is that integration's lunar n-dot
(entry 166), so it is the set's, whichever of its files is read: the moon
files first, the lunar ephemeris's own number as at J2000, then the planet
files (bug 166's case), the span nearest J2000 first, the file kept open
being then the one most calculations read. Read where the J2000 files are
read, by the path setter, it is published with the path and every reader
has it from the first call, the getter too. Reading instead, at the first
delta t, the file of that instant (bug 165's way for JPL) would leave the
getter, which has no instant, on the default, and a delta t at an
instant with no file (1900 here) on whatever moon file a calculation had
left open: -25.80 fresh, -25.936 after a Moon in 1500.

**Fix, as done here** (under `SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`'s `#ifndef`; the compat
build keeps upstream's default term):
- `ephe_path_read_moon()`, when neither J2000 file's header was found,
  looks for the other spans' moon files, nearest J2000 first, then their
  planet files (`ephe_path_read_other()`): each name looked up along the
  path as `swi_fopen()` finds it, but not opened (bug 118's
  `file_on_path()`), the first found opened, its header read and kept open
  with the span it answers for (bug 89), its DE number published as the
  J2000 file's (`sweph_denum_moon`, or bug 166's `sweph_denum_planet`), so
  the setters, the same path again, bug 107's first use, bug 131's reading
  after `swe_close()` and every thread and context taking the path carry
  it. A file the same path again finds open, or kept as the spare, is
  taken as it is.
- Bug 110's first-call warning ("Please call swe_set_ephe_path() ...") is
  not due where the default path holds such a file: `swi_ephe_path_none()`
  takes the planet file the path read too, as it took the moon file. With
  a working directory holding semo_12.se1 and sepl_12.se1, or sepl_12.se1
  alone, and no path set, the first `swe_deltat_ex()` in AD 1500 answered
  291.693033 s with the warning; now 294.255183 without it. With no Swiss
  file there it is due as before.
- Now delta t, `swe_deltat()`, the getter, the first and second Moon in
  AD 1500 and the heliocentric Mars there answer bit for bit as EPHEDIR,
  in both directories, on every reader.
- The opens, `fopen()` and `stat()` interposed, 100 rounds after a
  warm-up, before and after. Without the J2000 files (and with semo_12.se1
  and sepl_12.se1 alone): a path and two Swiss Moons in 1500, 4 calls and
  2 opens both, 0 stat() calls before and 1 after; 100 path changes, each
  with a Moon, 400 and 200 both, 100 stat() after (the setter opens
  semo_12.se1, which the Moon then reads); the same path again and a Moon
  0 both. With the other spans' planet files alone and a heliocentric
  Mars in 1900 (no file there): a path change 400 calls and no open
  before, 500 and 100 after (sepl_12.se1, as a fresh process given that
  path opens it), 5100 stat() calls; the same path again 400 calls and no
  open both, 5000 stat() calls (bug 118's look for a moon file installed
  since, 50 names; the planet file found as the spare). EPHEDIR's counts
  unchanged. In a directory with no Swiss file at all every setter call,
  the same path again too, looks the 100 names up, 100 stat() calls a
  path element: a path and a Moshier Mars 66 us a round before, 220
  after. Not a calculation's hot path.

## 177. On Moshier the barycentric Sun's slot keeps what the files or JPL last left in it, and the Moshier paths that read it take that for their Sun: after a warm fallback the heliocentric Moon 0.41 deg off, Ceres 0.14, the deflection 1.66e-7 on Mercury

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: call order -- a Swiss request fallen to Moshier, the fallback allowed, after a Swiss call at another instant: the heliocentric Moon 0.41 deg off the same request in a fresh process, Ceres heliocentric 0.14, `swe_calc_orbel()`'s orbit about the Sun and Cupido under SEFLG_TRUEPOS 0.071 and 9.1e-3, the deflection 1.66e-7 on Mercury and 1.7e-9 on Mars -- on every thread and context)**
**Where:** upstream `swemplan.c` `swi_moshplan()` (the Earth saved, the barycentric Sun's slot not) and its readers in `sweph.c`: `deflect_light_site()` and `deflect_light_from()`, `app_pos_etc_moon()`, `sweph()` (an asteroid's ephemeris from the slot's), `swecalc()` (the fictitious bodies' Sun), `app_pos_etc_orbel()`; here `swemplan.c`: `swi_moshplan()`

Found by entry 168's work (the deflection's 1.7e-9 deg on `swe_calc()`'s
Mars, 3e-8 on `swe_nod_aps()`'s points). The files and JPL fill the
barycentric Sun's slot, `pldat[SEI_SUNBARY]`, with the Earth's; Moshier
fills the Earth's alone, its places heliocentric, the Sun the origin of
its frame (bug 109's note). The slot is zero in a fresh context, and an
explicit Moshier request after a Swiss one finds it emptied with the other
save areas by the ephemeris switch; but a Swiss request fallen to Moshier
keeps the Swiss Sun an earlier call left there, of its instant, and five
Moshier paths read the slot as their Sun:

  asteroids, the fictitious bodies, `swe_calc_orbel()` and the stars): the

- the heliocentric Moon (`app_pos_etc_moon()`), its observer and centre;
- an asteroid read from its file takes the slot's ephemeris for its own
  (`sweph()`), so a heliocentric one had the slot's Sun taken off it as if
  barycentric (`app_pos_etc_plan()`);
- the fictitious bodies' heliocentric elements were made barycentric with
  it (`swecalc()`, `swi_osc_el_plan()`), and so `swe_calc_orbel()`'s orbit
  about the Sun (`app_pos_etc_orbel()`): the light time reads them again
  at t, SEFLG_TRUEPOS keeps the first.

## 183. Owen 1990's pieces step at their joins, and the frame's rates difference them across: the obliquity's 2.6e-8 deg/day off the day before -10000, the precession's 9.8e-9 and 1.1e-8 deg/day either side of +6000 and +14000, SEFLG_SPEED3 1.1e-4

Entry 159's noticed item. Owen 1990's precession angles (`owen_pre_matrix()`)
and mean obliquity (`epsiln_owen_1986()`) are Chebyshev fits in five
pieces of 80 centuries, centred on -14000, -6000, 2000, 10000 and 18000,

(`get_owen_t0_icof()`, the midpoint's own instant the later piece's): JD
-1931455.5, 990544.5, 3912544.5 and 6834544.5, about -10000, -2000, +6000
and +14000. The pieces do not meet. Measured as the second difference
over 2^-20 day at each join: the mean obliquity 0.0945 mas (2.63e-8 deg)
at -10000, the precession matrix 0.0860 mas (2.39e-8 deg, a unit vector's
largest displacement) at +6000 and 0.0908 mas (2.52e-8) at +14000, and
nothing else (both continuous to 1e-14 deg at -2000, the obliquity at
+6000 and +14000, the precession at -10000); the same under SEFLG_JPLHOR,
whose Owen 1990 differs by a constant. Owen 1990 is taken as the
long-term model ("0,10") and by SEFLG_JPLHOR's models outside 1799 Jan 1
.. 2202 Jan 1 (and with SEFLG_JPLHOR_APPROX under `SEMOD_JPLHORA_3`
before 1799). The rates entry 153 made keep to one side were told of no
such step: the precession's (P(t + 1) - P(t - 1)) / 2 (entry 49) and the
site's, the obliquity's eps(t + 1) - eps(t), and SEFLG_SPEED3's three
places over 1e-4 day. Against five-point differences of `swi_precess()`
and `swi_epsiln()` over 2^-6 day on the instant's side (G139's check (b)),
the worst over the day before the join and the day after: the obliquity's
rate 2.63e-8 deg/day the day before -10000, the precession's 9.80e-9
either side of +6000 and 1.09e-8 either side of +14000, alike under

differences of the positions over 2^-6 day on the instant's side: Mars
1.11e-8 deg/day at +6000 and 8.4e-9 at +14000, the Sun 9.9e-9 at +6000
and 5.9e-9 the day before -10000 (its latitude), the Moon's ecliptic
speeds 2.06e-8 the day before -10000; SEFLG_SPEED3 on Mars 1.11e-4 at
+6000 and 1.30e-5 at -10000.

**Fix, as done here:** `swi_frame_step_side()` (entries 153, 159, 160)
takes each Owen piece as a model of its own (`frame_owen_piece()`, by
`get_owen_t0_icof()` itself), wherever its models name Owen 1990:

side, and entry 153's one-sided differences take each piece's own rate.
The test reaches the models when the long-term model is Owen 1990 too;
the default models and flags read one more model number. Behind

- No hot path: one more model number read in the test.

## 184. The Moshier Moon's frame turning differences the frame across a short-term precession window's edges: its speed 8.7e-5 deg/day off within a day either side, its position 1.4e-9 deg through the light time

**Severity: Correctness (on Moshier with `SE_MODEL_PREC_SHORTTERM` set to IAU 1976 or 2000 and another long-term model, within a day of J2000 -+ 2 centuries: the Moon's speeds 8.0e-5 to 9.0e-5 deg/day off, the topocentric Moon's alike, its apparent place 1.36e-9 deg)**
**Where:** `swemmoon.c`: `swi_moshmoon()`

Entry 160's noticed item. Entry 95 made the Moshier Moon's velocity the
series' own derivative turned into the J2000 equator, plus the frame's
turning R'(t) x, taken as (R(t + 1) x - R(t - 1) x) / 2, R the
ecliptic-of-date-to-J2000 rotation of `ecl_equ2000_cart()` (the obliquity
with the cache's flags, the precession with none). R steps where the
precession or the obliquity changes model (entry 160: with IAU 1976 short
and Vondrak long, "0,9,1", 0.53" and 0.57" in the precession at J2000 -+
2 centuries, 3.4 and 81.6 mas in the obliquity), and the difference
reached across: for t within a day of the edge either side, R(t -+ 1)
was the other model's. Against five-point differences of the positions
over 2^-6 day on the instant's side (G139's), Moshier, "0,9,1" with the
IERS 2010 sidereal time: at + 2 centuries the Moon's ecliptic speeds
8.68e-5 deg/day off the day before (inside) and 8.69e-5 the day after,
equatorial 9.02e-5; at - 2 centuries 8.04e-5 and 8.32e-5; the topocentric
Moon (a nine-point difference over 2^-7 day, delta t 2^-11) 8.80e-5 and
9.04e-5. The apparent Moon is read at t - tau and carried there by its
velocity (entry 53), so its place took tau times the error, 1.36e-9 deg
in longitude within a day of the edge (tau 1.5e-5 day), and at the + 2
centuries edge - 1 day, whose reference reaches those places, the speed
5.1e-8 off them. The Owen 1990 joins (entry 183) lie outside Moshier's
range but at -2000, where the pieces meet; IAU 2006's window edges at -+
75 centuries outside it too.

**Fix, as done here:** where `swi_frame_step_side()` says the frame's
models change within a day of t -- the precession's with no flags, else
the obliquity's with the cache's, as `ecl_equ2000_cart()` takes them --
the frame's turning is the three-point derivative on t's side, s (4 R(t +
s) x - 3 R(t) x - R(t + 2s) x) / 2, s = -+1 day, as entry 153's
precession rate. Elsewhere the central difference, unchanged; the test
returns at once under the default models. Behind `#ifndef
SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT` (entry 95's derivative is this fork's; the compat

## 185. The equinox-of-date frame turning of the JDATE fictitious bodies and `swe_calc_orbel()` differences the frame across a short-term precession window's edges: Selena's speed 8.0e-5 to 9.5e-5 deg/day off within a day either side, Vulcan's up to 1.6e-5

**Severity: Correctness (with `SE_MODEL_PREC_SHORTTERM` set to IAU 1976 or 2000 and another long-term model, or with Owen 1990 at its joins: within a day of the step, as seen at the emission instant, the speed of every seorbel.txt body of the equinox of date (JDATE) and of every `swe_calc_orbel()` orbit of SE_ORBEL_EQ_DATE off by the frame's difference across it, Selena's 8.0e-5 to 9.5e-5 deg/day, an Earth orbit of 0.053 AU 8.0e-5 to 8.7e-5, a Sun orbit of 1.2 AU 3.8e-5 to 4.9e-5, Vulcan 4.6e-6 to 1.6e-5)**

ecliptic-of-date-to-J2000 rotation (`swi_epsiln()` and `swi_precess()`,
no flags), at tequ, the instant the elements are evaluated at -- under

difference, unchanged; the test returns at once under the default
models. Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: the fictitious bodies'

## 188. The IAU 2000A and 2000B series' arguments are evaluated in double, some 1e14" past 4e8 days: dpsi 9.5e-9 deg off the series at 8e8 to 1e9 days, jittering by 4e-9 from one instant to the next

**Severity: Correctness (the nutation, `swe_calc(SE_ECL_NUT)` and everything of date that takes it, past |J| 4e8 days, 1.1 million years: under the default, which is the direct IAU 2000A there (entry 152), and IAU 2000A or 2000B set explicitly, dpsi up to 9.5e-9 deg off a correctly rounded evaluation at 8e8 to 1e9 days, 3.0e-9 at 6e8 to 8e8, 4.9e-10 at 4e8 to 6e8; its rate 3.9e-9 deg/day, under the floor)**
**Where:** `swephlib.c`: `calc_nutation_iau2000ab()`, `calc_nutation_2000a_derivs()`, `calc_nutation_2000b_rate()`, new `nut_ls_args_exact()`

Entries 152's and 163's noticed item. The luni-solar series' Delaunay
arguments (Simon et al. 1994) are polynomials in T to T^4, in arcseconds,
evaluated in double and then reduced mod 360 deg. At |J - J2000| = 1e9
days (T = 27400) they are some 1e14" (the T^4 term of the Moon's mean
anomaly, 0.0002447 T^4, 1.4e14"): their last bit is 1.6e-2", and T itself,
rounded to a double, carries 4 c4 T^4 dT/T into them, 0.06" in the Moon's
mean anomaly, 0.015" in the node's; the constants as doubles and each
product's rounding add their own. Each term's angle is off by that, and
the main terms' amplitudes reach some 500" there through their T terms
(-0.0174"/cy on the 18.6-year term), so dpsi takes some 1e-8". Measured on
Moshier, `swe_calc(SE_ECL_NUT)` against the series transcribed in long
double (the arguments from J exactly, the constants read as long double,
every operation in it), 100 instants a band of |J - J2000|, either sign,
dpsi and deps, deg:
- IAU 2000A set explicitly: 4.9e-10 and 1.1e-10 at 4e8 to 6e8 days,
  3.0e-9 and 2.5e-10 at 6e8 to 8e8, 9.5e-9 and 6.2e-10 at 8e8 to 1e9; 1e-12
  at 1e7, 5.0e-11 at 2e8 to 4e8;
- IAU 2000B alike: 4.7e-10, 3.0e-9, 7.0e-9 in dpsi;
- the default: the grid's within 4e8 (9.2e-11), the direct 2000A's beyond
  (2.3e-9 at 6e8 to 8e8, 7.7e-9 at 8e8 to 1e9).
It is a jitter, not a bias: the places' fourth differences over 2^-12 day
/ sqrt(70), where the terms' own curvature is 1e-16 deg, are 3.6e-10 at
4e8 to 6e8, 1.8e-9 at 6e8 to 8e8 and 5.3e-9 to 7.8e-9 at 8e8 to 1e9. The
rate (`swi_nutation_rate()`, the series' own derivative there, entry
163) against five-point differences of the long double series over 2^-6
day: 3.2e-9 to 3.9e-9 deg/day at 8e8 to 1e9 days, under the floor. Only
the nutation reaches such dates (entry 152), and with it `SE_ECL_NUT`, the
sidereal time and the houses.

**Fix, as done here:** past |J| = 4e8 days (`SWI_NUT_ARGS_JMIN`, the
grid's bound), `nut_ls_args_exact()` evaluates the five arguments in
double-double: T from J exactly (J - J2000 by an exact sum, the quotient's
remainder by `fma()`), each constant as its double and the remainder of
its decimal value (`nut_ls_dd[]`), Horner's products by `fma()`, then
reduced modulo 1296000" exactly (`fmod()` of the high part, the low part
added) and made radians. `calc_nutation_iau2000ab()` takes them for M,
SM, F, D and OM (the planetary arguments, linear and some 2e8 rad, are
off by 3e-8 rad on terms of 3e-4", 1e-11"), and so do the rates,
`calc_nutation_2000a_derivs()` (the grid's node function, the rate past
4e8) and `calc_nutation_2000b_rate()`, so the rate stays the derivative of
the places. Within 4e8 days nothing changes, bit for bit: the double
evaluation there is within 1.2e-10 deg, and the step where the two meet
at 4e8 is that. Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`.
- After: within 3.0e-12 deg of the long double series in every band past
  4e8 days, under 2000A, 2000B and the default (3.5e-13 at 4e8 to 6e8;
  the long double reference's own arguments are good to 5e-6" at 1e9,
  3e-12 deg), fourth differences 4e-15 (2000A, the planetary terms'
  arguments) and 1e-16 (2000B); the rate within 2.2e-10 to 4.2e-10
  deg/day of the reference's five points over 2^-6 day at 8e8 to 1e9
  (its own rounding over the step: over 2^-8, 5.8e-10 to 7.9e-10).
- At absurd dates the answers are as finite or as NaN as before (1e72
  deg at 1e82 days, NaN from about 1e84 either way).
- Cost, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, bench's calc-moseph and
  calc-swieph (one repetition), the default models, whose grid evaluates
  its node function once a day: 23339446249 and 12271659405 before,
  23340363721 and 12272577309 after (+0.004%, +0.007%).

G140 `tests/nutderiv.c`, extended: check (c), SE_ECL_NUT under the
default, IAU 2000A and IAU 2000B at 64 instants with |J - J2000|
log-uniform over 4.1e8..1e9 days, either sign: the fourth differences

before the fix), 4.85e-9 compat. G29's numbers are the tip's (0.5714 and
0.2129 uas at |J| 1e7..1e13).

Noticed, not fixed:

  its flags, no error: on Moshier dpsi 1.2e72 deg at J = 1e82, NaN dpsi
  and deps from about 1e84 days (the arguments' T^4 overflows), under
  every nutation model, both builds, before and after this fix.

## 194. `swe_calc()`'s strict test of a Moon from Moshier reads the centre off the caller's bits: SEFLG_TOPOCTR with SEFLG_HELCTR or SEFLG_BARYCTR answers from the Earth of Moshier's Moon, and a SEFLG_TOPOCTR request after it from the save area

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: an answer where the strict setting refuses, and an answer that depends on call order; the place 9e-10 deg off the files')**
**Where:** `sweph.c`: `swe_calc_r_body()`, bug 120's test

Found by a review of entry 120's test. Entry 120 refuses, under
the strict setting, an answer that depends on a Moon taken from Moshier
for want of the semo file: the Moon and the Earth themselves and any body
seen from the Earth; a heliocentric or barycentric planet reads the Earth
but does not use it, and answers. `swe_calc_r()` told the two apart by the
caller's bits, `iflag & (SEFLG_HELCTR | SEFLG_BARYCTR)`. `swecalc()` resolves
the bits first by `plaus_iflag()`, where SEFLG_TOPOCTR turns SEFLG_HELCTR
and SEFLG_BARYCTR off: SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_HELCTR is a topocentric
request, seen from the Earth made from Moshier's Moon, and the test let it
through. In a directory without the semo files, strict, the site at 8.55
E, 47.37 N, 400 m, Mars at 1900 Jan 0.75 (JD 2415020.25) with SEFLG_SWIEPH
| SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_HELCTR (or SEFLG_BARYCTR) returned 32770 and
283.6744143987 deg, the complete directory's 283.6744143978 (9e-10 deg),
where SEFLG_TOPOCTR alone is refused ("Swiss (.se1) Moon file is not
available ..."). The answer stayed in the save area under the resolved
flags, SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_SWIEPH, so a SEFLG_TOPOCTR request after it in
the same context was answered, 32770 with the same place, where a fresh
process refuses it. The same for the Sun with SEFLG_TOPOCTR |
SEFLG_BARYCTR. `swe_calc_ut()`, the star functions and `swe_calc_orbel()`
resolve the bits before their tests and refused already. The compat build
has no entry 120 and answers all of them.

**Fix, as done here:** the test takes the resolved centre: SEFLG_TOPOCTR
counts as seen from the Earth whatever other centre bit is set, as
`plaus_iflag()` has it. The combined request is refused with entry 120's
message and leaves nothing in the save area (entry 120's
`sd->tsave = SWI_TJD_NEVER`), so the SEFLG_TOPOCTR request after it is
refused as in a fresh process; with the fallback allowed both answer, the
second bit for bit as in a fresh context. Inside entry 120's
`#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT` block. No hot path: one bit test on a path
taken only when a Moon came from Moshier.

`swe_nod_aps()` makes its save area by `swe_calc()` of the body with
SEFLG_HELCTR and the caller's SEFLG_TOPOCTR, so under the strict setting,
the semo files missing, its topocentric points are refused now too (Mars's
osculating node at 1900 had answered, 4.19e-9 deg off the files', Venus's
1.20e-8), as entry 120 refuses what is seen from that Earth. Its geocentric
points still answer (below).

G117 `tests/moonfile.c`: (a) and (a) warm take Mars with SEFLG_TOPOCTR |
SEFLG_HELCTR and with SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_BARYCTR and the Sun with the
latter, refused fresh and warm, answered Swiss with the note and within
1e-6 deg with the fallback allowed, answered as asked by the complete
directory; new (e): in one context Mars with each combination, then
SEFLG_TOPOCTR alone, the second's return and place bit for bit those of
SEFLG_TOPOCTR in a fresh context, strict and with the fallback allowed, at
the four instants. 472 rows pass; before the fix 44 fail (the 12 fresh
and 24 warm combined rows of (a), (e)'s 8 strict); the upstream build 212
(160 of the 372 before). G24 `moshmoon_topohel_ret`: Mars at 1900 Jan 0.75
with SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_HELCTR, the semo files missing, strict, its
return: -1 shipped, 32770 compat (and shipped before the fix). G133 and
G143 pass.

Noticed, not fixed: `swe_nod_aps()` has no test of entry 120's own: its
geocentric points, built from the save area's Earth made from Moshier's
Moon, answer under the strict setting, the semo files missing (Mars's
osculating node at 1900 4.19e-9 deg off the files', Venus's 1.20e-8),
where `swe_calc()`'s geocentric planets are refused. G117's header said
156 for the compat build's failures; the tree before this entry gives 160
(the topocentric row's note, lost there).

## 195. A topocentric star fallen to another ephemeris places its site by the delta t of the ephemeris asked: Aldebaran at 1500, Swiss fallen to Moshier, 2.0e-8 deg in longitude and 1.35e-7 deg/day in its speed off the Moshier request

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: an answer that depends on the ephemeris asked, not the one that answered; 2.0e-8 deg in place, 1.35e-7 deg/day in speed)**
**Where:** `sweph.c`: `fixstar_calc_from_struct()`, `swi_fixstar_calc_from_record()`, `fixstar_obs_rate()`

Found by entry 177's work (its notes). The star functions read the Earth
by `main_planet_bary()`, which falls from JPL to the Swiss files and from
the files to Moshier on its own; the return flag says the ephemeris that
answered (entry 67), and the parallax, deflection and aberration take that
Earth. The topocentric site did not: `swi_get_observer()` takes its delta t
by `swe_deltat_ex()` of the flags passed, and the star functions passed
the caller's, so a request fallen to Moshier placed Moshier's Earth's site
by the files' delta t (the files' tidal term, DE441's -25.936, against
Moshier's -25.58: 6.7 s more at 1500 with the planet files of 1800-2400,
4.1 s with no files, whose default is DE431's). `swe_calc()` places a
planet's site by the ephemeris that answered (its flags are `main_planet()`'s
after the fallback), and `swe_nod_aps()` since entry 168.

Measured, the site at 8.55 E, 47.37 N, 400 m, the fallback allowed, a
directory of links to sepl_18.se1, semo_18.se1, seas_12.se1, sefstars.txt
and seorbel.txt, Aldebaran with SEFLG_TOPOCTR | SEFLG_SPEED against the
same call asking SEFLG_MOSEPH:

| call | at 1500 (JD 2268923.5) | at 1338 (JD 2210000.25) |
|---|---|---|
| `swe_fixstar2()`, `swe_fixstar()` | 1.97e-8 deg in longitude, 9.4e-9 in latitude; 1.35e-7 deg/day in the longitude speed | 1.48e-8 deg, 3.23e-7 deg/day |
| `swe_fixstar2_ut()`, `swe_fixstar_ut()` | 2.02e-8 deg, 1.32e-7 deg/day | 1.69e-8 deg, 3.19e-7 deg/day |

The UT forms redo the call with Moshier's delta t for the instant, and
the site inside took the files' again. With a user delta t
(`swe_set_delta_t_userdef()`) the two agree to the last bit. With
sefstars.txt and seorbel.txt alone, 1.22e-8 deg and 8.3e-8 deg/day at
1500, 2.1e-10 deg at 1900, 0 at 2000. A JPL request fallen to the Swiss
files (de200.eph named and missing) took the JPL bits' delta t: 7.5e-9 deg
and 5.2e-8 deg/day off the Swiss request at 1500. A geocentric star has no
site and was bit for bit. Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:** the site's flags are the caller's with the
ephemeris bits of the Earth that answered: the observer at the instant and
`fixstar_obs_rate()`'s two observers for the aberration's rate (a new
argument). A Moon from Moshier on the files' Earth, the Moon files alone
missing (entry 120), keeps the files' delta t, as `swe_calc()`'s planets
do there. Now the fallen requests answer bit for bit as the Moshier (or
Swiss) request, return and place, all four functions, with and without
SEFLG_SPEED, fresh and warm. Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`; no hot
path (the star functions, one flag computed per topocentric call).

## 170. `swe_nod_aps_ut()` takes delta t from the ephemeris bits as given, and keeps it after a fallback

**Severity: Correctness (behaviour: the points at another instant than the ephemeris that answered puts UT at; 2.8e-7 deg on Mars's perihelion, 3.6e-5 deg on the Moon's), both builds**
**Where:** `swecl.c`: `swe_nod_aps_ut_r_body()`, `swe_nod_aps_r_body()`

Found by entry 149's work. `swe_nod_aps_ut()` was `swe_nod_aps()` at
tjd_ut + `swe_deltat_ex(tjd_ut, iflag)`, the caller's bits as given.
`swe_calc_ut()` (and `swe_calc_orbel_ut()`, `swe_fixstar_ut()`,
`swe_pheno_ut()`) resolves the bits first and, when the answer's
ephemeris is not the one asked, takes delta t again from the one that
answered and computes again; `swe_nod_aps()` returned no flag to say
which. Measured:
- Fallen to Moshier, the fallback allowed, it kept the files' delta t: in
  an empty directory at 1900 Jan 0.75 UT -1.9915 s for Moshier's -2.0521 s
  (the default tidal term against DE404's), Mars's osculating perihelion
  2.8e-7 deg off the Moshier request's, the Moon's osculating perigee
  1.7e-6, its mean node 3.7e-8 (which reads no file, and since entry 174
  falls back from nothing).
- `swe_deltat_ex()` takes SEFLG_SWIEPH with SEFLG_JPLEPH for the Swiss
  files' tidal term ("SEFLG_SWIEPH wanted or SEFLG_JPLEPH failed"): on
  de200, SEFLG_JPLEPH | SEFLG_SWIEPH, answered from DE200, took DE431's
  delta t for DE200's, the Moon's topocentric osculating points at 1900
  3.6e-5 deg off the SEFLG_JPLEPH request's, Mars's 2.7e-6.
Both builds.

**Fix, as done here:**
- `swe_nod_aps_r_body()` says which ephemeris answered: the less precise
  of its reads where they differ (the osculating ellipse's, the save
  area's), as `swe_calc_pctr()` returns it (entry 150); a Moon from
  Moshier, the Moon files alone missing, SEFLG_MOSEPH, as `swe_calc()`
  flags it (entry 120).
- `swe_nod_aps_ut()` as `swe_calc_ut()`: one ephemeris bit by
  `plaus_iflag()`'s precedence (Swiss without one), delta t of it, and if
  another answered, delta t of that one and the points computed again, the
  first call's message kept.
- Now the fallback's UT points are the Moshier request's bit for bit, and
  the mixed bits' those of the ephemeris they resolve to.
- Behind `#ifndef SWE_UPSTREAM_COMPAT`: upstream answers so. No hot path.

Mars, mean and osculating, the four centres, both instants and the four
bit combinations against the ephemeris they resolve to, bit for bit: 128
